Header: Bemisia tabaci (Sudu Messa in Sinhala Language, VenEe in Tamil Language)

Prevention: Remove old plantations completely and destroy crop residues by burning before planting new.
Keep the field away from old cultivations.
Encourage natural enemies (ladybugs, lacewing larvae) by maintaining vegetation ground cover below papaya.
Eradicate other hosts such as “Hulanthala" and wild sunflower prior to planting and later on.
Sow maize around the field (2-3 lines) to prevent white flies immigrating from other fields.
Monitoring: Observe plants regularly from the initial stage of crop.
Look for whiteflies on the lower surface of leaves specially in dry weather.
Observe whiteflies flying around the infected plants.
Observe leaf curling with many whiteflies below.
Look for honeydew associated sooty moulds and dull looking leaves.
Papaya can tolerate quite some whiteflies.
But consider starting control measures at the time of presenting 3 to 10 whiteflies per leave per plant.
Direct Control: Remove and burn severely infected leaves.
Some whiteflies will fly away, but young ones and eggs cannot move.
Use 4-5 trap/acre at yellow sticky traps above 10 cm above the foliage to suppress the population.
Wash off plants with a strong stream of water to wash off whiteflies.
Spray neem seed extract (50g seeds soak and crush and add 1L of water and keep it for 24 hrs, dilute 1:5 and spray).
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re- entry interval.
Do not empty into drains and water sources.
